sources.note: Nothing: a language-ecosystem / vitality survey (settlements, speaker numbers, L2 repertoires, migrations, domains, attitudes). a full-text search for stress/accent over the 62-page text finds no 'accent', 'tone', 'tonal', 'prosod', 'syllable' (except an 1870 primer title in the references) and 'stress' only in 'We also stress how important it is' (p.229); 'phonolog' only in the reference to Rangelov's COOL13 talk title. sources.citation: Guy, J. B. M. 1980. Glottochronology without cognate recognition. Pacific Linguistics, Series B-79. Canberra: Department of Linguistics, Research School of Pacific Studies, Australian National University. viii+134 pp.
sources.note: No phonology content for Vunapu. The one relevant remark, p.5: 'The lists are furthermore not phonemicized, and it might have been preferable to select lists elicited by myself (such as Vunapu, Tolomako, Roria, etc.) the originals of which were, unlike their published versions, phonemicized.' -- i.e. Guy holds (held) a phonemicized original Vunapu wordlist that Tryon 1976 did not print as such; confirms the works still to obtain 'Guy field wordlist' and that the published forms are sub-phonemic. The only 'stress' token in the book (stress placement in a Sesake/Tongoa example *amtas) concerns…

sources.citation: Guy, Jacques B. M. 1978. Proto-North New Hebridean reconstructions. In S. A. Wurm & Lois Carrington (eds), Second International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics: Proceedings, 781-850. Pacific Linguistics C-61. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-C61.781
sources.note: Nothing for Vunapu. General: 'Word-stress does not seem to have existed in PNNH as it appears to have been innovated along different rules in Sakao, Lehali, and Shark Bay' (p.782); Tolomako section: 'Stress was innovated on the penultimate vowel and posttonic non-high vowels often assimilated to non-high tonic' (txt l.172); Sakao section stage 2: 'Word-stress is innovated. If we define a syllable nucleus as V or VV, stress most often affected the penultimate syllable' (txt l.435-436).
